rationale: The Latin anchors *rusticus* (rustic/peasant) and *colonus* (farmer/tenant) firmly point to a rural, agricultural sense rather than mere national identity. OE *ceorl* denotes a free peasant or husbandman living in the country, which aligns directly with countryman.n.02 ("a man who lives in the country and has country ways"), not the patriotic/national sense of countryman.n.01.
